cleanIntro: This is Carl Walther's own P38 book, and the P38 it describes is the P38 you have: same barrel catch lever on the left of the frame, same locking wedge under the barrel, same slide-mounted safety that drops the hammer, same four main assemblies. The book is a post-war Ulm printing, so two details are worth holding lightly - it tabulates a light-metal frame, and it describes the loaded-chamber signal pin as though every gun has one. Neither is true of every surplus P38, and this guide says where.

steps.title: Safety catch on, muzzle down - the rule for the whole session
steps.action: While the pistol is being loaded, unloaded or disassembled, the safety catch is engaged and the muzzle points at the ground. Walther adds that disassembly of the main components needs no tools and leaves no loose small parts.
steps.prose: Engaging the P38's safety does three things at once: it blocks the firing pin, releases the hammer from its notch and lets it fall onto a blocked pin. That is the state the gun should be in from the moment it reaches the bench, and the one you check first if anything about the strip feels wrong.
steps.quote: While the pistol is being loaded, unloaded or disassembled, ensure that the safety catch is engaged and the muzzle is pointing towards the ground. Disassembly of the pistol’s main components requires no tools and there are no loose small parts.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — Instructions for handling and using the P 38, printed p.8 (OCR page 5)

steps.title: Magazine catch back, magazine out
steps.action: Push back the magazine catch and remove the magazine.
steps.prose: The P38's magazine catch is at the heel of the butt, not a button behind the trigger guard, and it pushes rearward. If you are used to modern pistols this is the control that will not be where your thumb goes looking for it. Two hands: one on the catch, one under the magazine so it does not drop on concrete.
steps.quote: Push back the magazine catch and remove the magazine (fig. 4).
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — Loading the pistol, printed p.8 (OCR page 5)

steps.title: Slide back to the stop, then look into the chamber
steps.action: Draw the slide back up to the stop so the chambered round is extracted and ejected, remove the magazine, and make a visual check that the chamber is clear.
steps.prose: All the way to the stop. The P38's extractor will pull a case out on a short stroke and then let it fall back in, which is exactly the failure that leaves someone certain an empty gun is empty. Walther's own unloading sequence has you hold the magazine out a finger's breadth with your little finger while you rack, so nothing feeds behind the round you just removed.
steps.quote: Pull the magazine out a finger’s breadth and secure with your little finger (see fig. 11). Draw back the slide up to the stop.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — Unloading the pistol, printed p.14 (OCR page 8)
steps.warn: Remove the magazine. Make visual check that chamber is clear!

steps.title: Check whether YOUR P38 has the signal pin - do not assume it
steps.action: The book describes a signal pin above the hammer which can be both felt and seen and which indicates a cartridge in the chamber. Look at the back of your slide above the hammer and establish whether yours actually has one.
steps.prose: This is the one place a surplus gun can genuinely differ from the book in front of you, and it is why the check is a step rather than a footnote. Whatever you find, the pin is never the unloading check - looking into the chamber is. Treat a signal pin as a convenience and a missing one as normal.
steps.quote: The signal pin (21) above the hammer, which can be both felt and seen, indicates that there is a cartridge in the chamber.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — The functions of the trigger and safety mechanism, Fig. 18, printed p.23 (OCR page 12)

steps.title: Safety applied, magazine out, chamber proved - then and only then
steps.action: Apply the safety catch. Check whether the pistol is loaded by removing the magazine and ensuring that no round is chambered. That is Walther's own opening line for the strip and there is no shortcut past it.
steps.prose: The next move puts your palm over the muzzle while you press the butt down. That is the reason this check is not a formality on this particular pistol: you are about to put a hand in front of the barrel deliberately, so the chamber gets proved empty by eye and by finger first.
steps.quote: Disassembling the pistol Cal. 9 mm Apply the safety catch. Check whether the pistol is loaded by removing the magazine and ensuring that no round is chambered.

steps.title: Muzzle on something soft, butt down, barrel catch forward
steps.action: Press the muzzle of the barrel vertically down onto a soft surface and push the butt down to the stop. Now turn the barrel catch (51) towards the muzzle, up to the stop. Lift the barrel and slide assembly forward and off.
steps.prose: Pressing the butt down unloads the recoil springs so the catch can rotate; try to turn it without that and it will not move, and forcing it is how the catch gets damaged. Soft surface means a folded towel or a bench mat - the muzzle crown is carrying the whole weight of your push, and a marked crown is a marked group.
steps.quote: Press the muzzle of the barrel vertically down on to a soft surface and push the butt down to the stop. Now turn the barrel catch (51) towards the muzzle, up to the stop. Lift the barrel and slide assembly forward and off.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — Disassembling the pistol, printed pp.16-17 (OCR page 9)

steps.title: Push the locking pin in, barrel out the front of the slide
steps.action: Press in the locking pin (7) with your thumb. That opens the lock and lets the barrel be drawn forward out of the slide.
steps.prose: The pin is the head of the P38's locking wedge, sitting under the barrel behind the slide's mouth. A thumb is enough - there is no need for a punch and nothing needs to come out. The wedge stays with the barrel and the two locking lugs go with it.
steps.quote: Pressing in the locking pin (7) with the thumb opens the lock and allows the barrel to be removed from the front of the slide.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — Disassembling the pistol, printed p.18 (OCR page 10)

steps.title: Leave the recoil spring guides alone
steps.action: Do not force the recoil spring guides out of their seats in the frame, and do not push them in and let them shoot forward. Walther says both cause damage.
steps.prose: The guides sit in shallow recesses either side of the frame and the recesses are the part that breaks, not the guides. Once broken, the springs have nothing to bear against. Clean around them with a brush and leave them exactly where they are - there is no owner-level reason to remove them.
steps.quote: The recoil spring guides must not be forced out of their seats as this will damage the matching recesses opposite (see arrow). Do not push in the guides and then allow them to shoot forward as this will also cause damage.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — Disassembling the pistol, caution, printed p.18 (OCR page 10)

steps.title: Field strip complete - four assemblies, and that is the limit
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel with its locking wedge, and magazine. The pistol has now been separated into its four main component assemblies ready for cleaning, and Walther states that further stripping may only be carried out by an authorized gunsmith.
steps.prose: Everything routine is in front of you: the bore from either end, the locking lugs and their recesses in the slide, the breech face, the extractor and the frame rails. On a surplus gun this is also the moment to look for what the last eighty years did - peening on the lugs, a cracked slide at the rear, a worn hammer nose.
steps.quote: Further stripping may only be carried out by an authorized gunsmith.
steps.cite:
WALTHER Selbstladepistole Mod. P38
Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions / Notice d'emploi / Instrucciones de uso — P38 Bedienungsanleitung (DE/EN/FR/ES), 14pp — Disassembling the pistol, printed p.18 (OCR page 10)

steps.title: A surplus gun gets inspected, not just cleaned
steps.action: Walther asks that any pistol affected by corrosion, or damaged by being dropped, is inspected by a qualified gunsmith. On a gun of this age that is not an exceptional case - it is the default.
steps.prose: The P38's known wear points are the locking lugs and their recesses, the hammer and sear engagement, and cracking at the rear of the slide on hard-used examples. None of those is something a cleaning session fixes, but a cleaning session is when you would see them. If anything looks peened, cracked or out of shape, stop shooting it until someone competent has looked.

deepAbsentReason: Walther publishes nothing deeper for the P38 than the four-assembly strip. The disassembly page ends by saying the pistol has been separated into its four main component assemblies ready for cleaning and that further stripping may only be carried out by an authorized gunsmith; the rest of the book is loading, firing, the safety mechanism and a set of cutaway diagrams of the trigger and safety functions, which are illustrations rather than procedures. ⛔ PROHIBITED IS PER-PROCEDURE, NOT PER-FAMILY: what Walther bars is stripping further, and the whole published clean is walked above. The forbidden operation is carried in this spec's `prohibits` field. Nothing was invented to fill the gap - and on a seventy-year-old service pistol, inventing a lockwork procedure would be the worst possible place to start.

cleaning.name: BARREL, LOCKING WEDGE & LUGS
tasks: Brush the bore and follow with patches until they come out clean; an old barrel takes more passes than a new one and tells you less by feel
Clean the locking wedge under the barrel and both locking lugs, and look hard at their bearing faces for peening
Clean the corresponding recesses inside the slide - that pair of surfaces is what holds the breech shut
Wipe the chamber and check it for pitting; surplus guns fired with corrosive primers often have it

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & FIRING PIN CHANNEL
tasks: Clean the breech face and around the extractor without levering the extractor out of its seat
Brush the frame rails and the raceway, then wipe them dry before oiling
Clean around the recoil spring guides in place - do not force them out of their seats
Keep solvent out of the firing pin channel and make sure none is left standing in it

cleaning.name: OIL, MAGAZINE & STORAGE
tasks: A thin film of good quality oil on the metal with the excess wiped off; over-oiling an old gun just carries grit into the lockwork
A drop on the rails, on the locking wedge faces and on the barrel where the slide bears
Wipe the magazine inside and out and check the feed lips; surplus magazines are the most commonly worn part on these pistols
Do not store the pistol in leather or anything else that holds moisture against the finish

reassembly: Check first that nothing protrudes above the frame at the rear - the decocking piece, the ejector and the release lever must all be down, or the slide will not go on.
Insert the barrel fully into the slide.
Install the slide from the front of the frame, pushing up on the locking piece as it goes.
Once the slide is in place, stand the pistol on its muzzle again, push the frame down to the stop and turn the barrel catch back to the rear.
Assemble only with the safety catch engaged and the hammer decocked, and with no magazine in the butt.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: the barrel catch must be fully rotated to the rear and flush; the slide should run its full stroke and return to battery under both recoil springs evenly; the safety catch should drop the hammer with the firing pin blocked and the hammer must not reach the pin; the double-action pull should cock and drop the hammer smoothly and the single-action notch should hold at full cock without following when the slide is released briskly; and the slide should lock open on an empty magazine and release cleanly on the slide catch lever. On a surplus gun, add a look at the locking lugs and the rear of the slide every single time.
